newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST -- Italy Nov car registrations seen falling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -- Italy Nov car registrations seen falling.

text.p: Italian new car registrations in November are set to fall compared to year ago levels when registrations were inflated following the end of a car delivery truck drivers strike.

Industrial sources and analysts expect car registration figures, due on December 10 from the Ministry of Transport, will fall 10-12 percent to 130,000-132,000 units from 151,227 seen in November 1995, but this comes after a sharp rise in October in comparison to the strike-hit month of October 1995.
Taking the two months of October and November together, expectations are for a small rise over the same two months of 1995, they added.
"While in October the comparison month was weak because of the strike, now the comparison is inflated because of late deliveries after the strike," said one industrial source.

Last October, the strike of the drivers paralysed car deliveries for many days and led to car registrations of just 117,600 units. This lead to the rise of 20 percent in car registrations in October 1996 compared to October 1995.

"Now, we have the opposite situation. Last November, there were 151,000 registrations, inflated from October, and a figure of 130,000 this year will represent a fall that is not really there," said the source.

In relation to the two months of October and November 1995, when registrations were 268,800, there could be a rise of three percent to around 276,00 cars, based on a November figure of 132,000 and October of 144,000.
"The market remains flat. To speak one day of incentives and another day of no incentives is paralysing sales. Many prefer to wait for the start of the new year," said the source.
Looking to the whole of 1996, the source expected a small fall in overall sales compared to the 1.74 million sales in 1995. "I think 1.70 million units," he said.

Giampaolo Trasi, analyst at brokers IMI-Sigeco said, "The figures will show a fall of 12 percent from November 1995 to 132,000 due to the effect of the strike. While the two months will see a slight rise, it remains negative data."
According to Trasi, the small recovery in the two month figures are from hopes that the market has reach levels where it can not be squeezed down any further.
The negative market outlook was confirmed also by the industry forecasting body Centro Studi Promotor (CSP).

"For 1996, we think there will be a fall in registrations to 1.72 million from 1.74 million last year, and the data will be worse in 1997 with a fall to 1.68 million," said CSP's director Giamprimo Quagliano.
He added that a market improvement will only come from the introduction of incentives to buy new cars in exchange for scrapping cars older than 10 years.
With an incentive of 1.5 million lire per car in a incentive scheme, the market could rise to 1.938 million, Quagliano added.
